home.title: Zero to robotics engineer in 6 months
home.lead: Start by reading a schematic, end with ROS 2, control, perception and robot learning. Every lesson has an original explanation, hands-on tasks and curated resources — and your progress stays in your own browser.
home.how1: Each lesson opens with an original bilingual explanation: concepts, formulas and common mistakes on one page.
home.how2: Build circuits in the embedded Falstad simulator, run the example code from the repository, answer quizzes and tick off the task list.
home.how3: Resource cards link straight to the original courses, books and tools. Copyright stays with their authors.
home.progressLocal: Progress is stored only in this browser (localStorage) and never uploaded.

about.title: About & credits
about.lead: A study site built for actually learning — not a link dump.
about.source: The six-month structure, monthly goals, milestones and resource list come from @DeRonin_'s September 2026 article “How to become a Robotics Engineer in 6 months (RESOURCES)”. On top of that we wrote original explanations and exercises, and added a few resources (marked as supplements).
about.copyright: All external resources (courses, textbooks, videos, tools) belong to their authors or institutions. This site does not mirror or republish them; it only provides original summaries and links. The Falstad simulator is embedded from its official page via iframe.
about.privacy: No login, no tracking. Your progress lives only in your browser's localStorage.
about.safety: This course involves soldering irons, lithium batteries and other potentially dangerous tools. Solder in a ventilated space, wear eye protection, and never leave a LiPo charging unattended.
about.openSource: The site is open source on GitHub — issues and PRs welcome.

widget.label: Simplified model
widget.mirrors: Line-by-line port of the Python script:
widget.note: Same model as the simulated output above; real hardware values will differ.
widget.ignoreError: Distortion is being ignored; the pixel is off by {err} px.
widget.lineTitle: Line follower P/PD: starting 20 mm off the line
widget.cfTitle: Complementary filter: α, time constant and the offset from gyro bias
widget.cfApprox: Note: this widget is not a line-by-line port. The script adds random noise (Python's random, seed 7), which is not reproduced in the browser; this uses the analytic steady-state approximation of the same filter equation with a constant bias, offset ≈ α/(1−α)·bias·dt. It agrees with the script's offset_flat column only to 1 decimal place (0.1 / 0.7 / 3.0°), and the test checks agreement to 1 decimal place only.
widget.snapTitle: Snap-fit arm: strain and push-on force
widget.snapLocks: self-locking (μ·tan a ≥ 1, cannot be pushed on)
widget.snapFixed: Arm width b = 6 mm and friction μ = 0.3, the script's defaults.
widget.gearPlanetary: Planetary stage (ring fixed, sun in, carrier out)
widget.gearNoMesh: The planet would need {teeth} teeth, not a whole number: will not mesh
widget.gearNoSpace: {n} planets cannot be spaced evenly ((sun + ring) / {n} = {q})
widget.gearBacklash: Backlash at the joint → error at the tip
widget.stsLayout: 0xFF 0xFF  ID  LENGTH  INSTRUCTION  PARAMS…  CHECKSUM = ~(ID + LENGTH + INSTRUCTION + PARAMS) & 0xFF
widget.stsNotHex: not a list of hex bytes
widget.stsShort: too few bytes for a complete reply
widget.stsBadChecksum: bad checksum: the bytes were corrupted on the wire
